answer: A wharf charges every ship a docking fee before it can unload, and an agent economy can do the same: require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud. Like a willow bending under weight, cheap identities bend the system; a stake makes each fake identity cost real money, so spawning ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand stakes. A glacier moves slowly but crushes what stands in its path, and vesting the stake over time means an attacker must wait and pay while honest agents earn it back through useful work.
